newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Human smuggling from Bangladesh at alarming level.
newsitem.headline: Human smuggling from Bangladesh at alarming level.

text.p: About 200 Bangladeshi women and children are smuggled out of the country each day, and most end up as prostitutes, the Independent newspaper quoted activists as saying on Monday.
"Trafficking in women and children in Bangladesh has reached an alarming level," the newspaper quoted an activist as telling a workshop in Dhaka on Sunday.
Some 36 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) on Sunday launched an umbrella body, Traffic Watch Bangladesh (TWB), to monitor and lobby against human trafficking.
TWB said more than 200,000 Bangladeshi women and children had been smuggled to neighbouring countries, especially to Pakistan and India, mostly for prostitution.
About 30,000 Bangladeshi women were in different brothels in Calcutta, the capital of India's West Bengal state, which borders Bangladesh.
TWB said another 10,000 Bangladeshi children were trapped in brothels in India's Bombay and Goa.
"Besides prostitution, women and children are being used in the sale of human organs...bonded labour and even for polygamy," the Independent quoted Ishrat Shamim, a TWB activist, as saying.
Police and human rights activists say poor women and children are lured to foreign countries with fake promises of high paying jobs and sometimes marriage.
